who is the mother Alexander the Great? Kill her husband? It's really simple: If you're a king, you marry a lot of foreign women for alliances. Olympias is not Macedonian, so there are many people in the Macedonian court who dislike her. As a young man, Alexander was notorious for being a thug; he's very strategic, unlike Philip who is very deliberate. So Philip was worried about Alexander. Later, Philip married a Macedonian woman and they had a son together. What this means now is that this son is next in line to the throne, not Alexander. Olympias taught Alexander from day one that you are special: You're not the son of Philip II; you're the son of God.

Olympias felt that Philip II was about to steal the throne and had him killed. She also killed his new Macedonian wife and their son. Philip II's army, led by Alexander, will conquer Persia. His conquest path will take about 10 years, during which he moves quickly with a small army, showing cooperation from local elites. At this time in history, Persia is stagnant; there's competition between the upper and lower nobility. The low ability plot was probably helping Alexander conquer Persia.

Alexander saw himself as the new Achilles and had memorized the Iliad, taking it with him wherever he went. During his war, he took one of his enemies, tied him to the back of his chariot, and rolled the guy around, just like Achilles did to Hector. When visiting Egypt, he conquered it and then went to Ammon to visit an oracle. The oracle told him that he is not the son of Philip II but the son of God, Zeus Aman in Greek tradition and Amon in Egyptian tradition.

This explains why when Alexander conquered most of Persia, Darius offered him a billion dollars to go away, but he refused. After conquering Persepolis, which was the capital of the Persian Empire, he kept going to India because the only reason he stopped is that his soldiers got sick of fighting. Alexander was known for his atrocities; he burned down cities like Thebes and Persepolis, possibly as ritual sacrifices to prove he was a son of God.

These actions were not random; they served diplomatic and military purposes.
